---
title: "Pigeonhole Principle: Prove a Collision Is Unavoidable"
description: "An interview maths technique with symbols, numbers and an independent proof."
---

## When this technique appears

When proving a duplicate, shared bucket, remainder collision or guaranteed matching pair.

## The question

**What can be guaranteed without constructing a specific matching pair?**

## Formula worth memorising

$$
N>k\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists\text{ a bucket containing at least }2\text{ objects}
$$

**Every symbol explained:** N is the number of objects; k is the number of buckets; > means there are more objects than buckets; ∃ means there exists at least one bucket with two or more objects.

**Substitute actual numbers:** Put 5 socks into 4 labelled drawers. If every drawer held at most one, there could be at most 4 socks. Since there are 5, some drawer holds at least 2.

## Prove the mathematical step

Proof by contradiction: assume every bucket has at most one item. Summing over k buckets gives at most k objects, contradicting N>k. This is a lower-bound argument requiring no search.

## Common mistake or limitation

A duplicate bucket does not imply identical objects unless bucket definitions encode the right equivalence relation. Repeated hash values do not guarantee identical inputs.

## The 20-second memory card

**Memorise: Define buckets, count capacity if every bucket avoids collision, then show objects exceed capacity.**

Practise by speaking the argument, not reciting the formula alone.

**Interview problems:** Contains Duplicate; Remainder Collisions.
